text:
Sam W.: Quick idea — add a "quick switcher" flow where you hit `/` (or a button) on any per-route or per-model view and can: 1) save the current filters as a saved-query, 2) immediately create a lightweight alert from it, or 3) export an SDK snippet to fetch the same telemetry. low friction.

Julie (UX): I like it. Saves are often followed by 'now how do I alert on this'. Combine them. UX Q: do we force users to pick alert severity/template in the same modal or a follow-up step? :thinking_face:

Matt P.: From infra side, two things: 1) saved-query -> alert creation should reference query_id only, alert evaluation runs in alert service (not console). 2) exporting SDK snippet should include sampling and time window metadata, otherwise users get mismatched results.

Kevin (Infra): Also we need to be careful about telemetry cost. If quick-create for alerts defaults to a high sample rate it could blow up evaluation jobs. Suggest default sampling to the view's telemetry sample rate (if present) and a warning if user increases it.

Julie (UX): Proposed modal flow: primary action = Save query; secondary actions = "Create alert" (opt-in inline form) and "Export code" dropdown. Inline alert form should be compact: name, threshold, window, severity. Add a small "advanced" link for scheduling options.

Sam W.: Agree. For ownership: when user creates an alert from a saved-query, the saved-query stays with their team/route. Alert metadata should link to saved-query id and user id. We need RBAC check — only people with alert:create in that workspace can see the button.

Matt P.: RBAC is doable. On the API contract: saved-query create returns {id, spec_hash, sample_rate, retention_hint}. Alert-create should accept saved_query_id or the inline spec; if saved_query_id is passed, backend resolves sample_rate & spec immutably at creation time. That avoids surprises later if query changes.

Julie (UX): UX note: show a small toast "Alert created — evaluating in 2 mins" and a link to the alert page. Users expect confirmation. Also show estimated monthly eval cost if the sample_rate/interval chosen impacts cost. :money_with_wings:

Kevin (Infra): For cost estimate we can use the same estimator as the billing preview. Quick note: include quotas — orgs with low alert-eval quota should get disabled CTA with a tooltip.

Sam W.: On export SDK snippet, we should support both JS and Python. Example we can show:
```js
// JS snippet generated from saved query
const client = new RedwoodAnalytics({apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY});
const q = await client.fetchSavedQuery({id: "saved:12345", window: "5m", sample_rate: 0.01});
console.log(q.metrics);
```

Julie (UX): Nice. Keep snippets minimal and copyable. Also include a tiny checkbox in modal "Include credentials example" (off by default).

Matt P.: Two backend concerns: 1) freezing spec at alert creation (we discussed) 2) we need an audit log entry linking saved_query->alert creation for compliance. Add user, timestamp, and before/after snapshots.

Sam W.: Rollout plan: feature flag on console. Enable in staging for a few teams, gather metrics: saved-query->alert conversion rate, SDK exports, avg sample_rate chosen. We should add an experiment variant where the "Create alert" is default vs opt-in to measure conversion.

rollout-bot: Flag `quick-swap-save-alert` created by @Sam W. targeting orgs: staging-1, dev-squads. Scheduled rollout: 2025-06-03.

Kevin (Infra): Telemetry/metrics to emit: quick_switch_opened, save_query_clicked, create_alert_clicked, sdk_exported, alert_eval_cost_estimate_shown. Add properties: org_id, user_id (hashed), route_id, model_id, sample_rate, window. Keep event sizes small.

Julie (UX): One more UX edge: if the user opens quick switcher from a route that had inherited filters (team default + personal override), the modal should show which filters are inherited vs local and let them toggle inheritance before save. Avoid surprises.

Matt P.: API endpoint names proposal: POST /api/v1/saved_queries (body: spec, scope, metadata), POST /api/v1/alerts (body: saved_query_id | spec, threshold, window, eval_config). The alerts service will call saved_query.resolve_if_needed(). We'll add `frozen_spec` in alert record.

Sam W.: Sounds solid. Action items: Julie — mockups for modal + keyboard shortcut behavior; Matt — API contract sketch + example responses; Kevin — telemetry event schema + quota gating behavior; I'll wire up the feature flag and rollout plan.

Julie (UX): I'll drop 2 mockups by EOD tomorrow. Short and focused.

Matt P.: I'll post API proto later today.

Kevin (Infra): I'll add event schema PR and a quota error UX example.

Sam W.: Thanks team. If no objections, I'll enqueue this for next sprint refinement. :+1:
